thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT @channel — SLO breach detected for /v1/stream (us-west-2).
p95 = 420ms (SLO 300ms), p99 = 1.82s (SLO 900ms). Streaming stalls and tail spikes observed. Triggered at 2026-03-15T01:10:21Z

maria: I'm on it. Any customer 5xxs or errors?

dmitri: No 5xx flood, mostly timeouts and stall logs. Cache hitrate for prefix-cache jumped down 01:09 -> from 87% to ~22% across prod. Paging ops up x6.

kevin: dashboards: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/streams?panel=cache (live) — you can see the prefetch miss storm

maria: ok, suspected rollout? Which change landed 01:05?

dmitri: prefixhash rollout to v4 started 01:04 (canary -> ramp). telemetry shows non-monotonic hash seed switch in v4. Prefetch keys not matching, warmups ineffective. Cold miss flood hit paging layer and caused tail latency.

julia: CS report: two enterprise tenants reported slow streaming and one timed-out upload. Escalation opened (CS-6123).

maria: mitigation plan: 1) pause/rollback prefixhash rollout, 2) route streaming traffic to warm variant, 3) enable bypass-cache-for-longstreams flag. Can we get a quick rollback?

maria: @deploy-bot request: rollback prefixhash rollout id=pf-roll-389 -> v3
deploy-bot: Received rollback request. Verifying commit hashes...

kevin: router patch ready (preview):
```
# quick router override
patch /services/streaming/routes
  - match: /v1/stream
    action: route
    params:
      model: gpt-x-v1
      variant: warm
      fallback: compact
```
apply with: infractl route apply --file quick-route.yaml --env prod

maria: applying route then rollback. dmitri keep an eye on cache hitrate.

opsbot: Flag flip: bypass-cache-for-longstreams=true applied to prod-pool-06.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: prefixhash-rollout pf-roll-389 -> restoring v3. Started 01:28:10Z. ETA ~90s.

dmitri: after bypass + route, immediate p99 improvement from 1.82s -> 1.05s in 2m. Cache hitrate slowly recovering as v3 restored. Paging ops dropping.

kevin: KV logs showing namespace mismatch around 01:07:
```
WARN  kvstore: lookup miss namespace=pf_v4 key=abc123
INFO  prefetch: scheduled_keys=0 window=30s
ERROR prefetch: miss_rate=0.78 window=120s
```
Hypothesis: v4 changed salt/seed causing different keyspace; prefetchers assumed continuity and invalidated warm caches.

julia: Customer impact summary: ~45 requests/min experienced >=1s latency spike in the 01:10-01:35 window; two enterprise tenants raised support tickets. No data loss, but SLA alerts fired. CS notified customers with temporary workaround.

maria: good, keep CS updated. We'll draft incident severity A since SLOs breached and customers hit.

dmitri: I'm taking the overnight watch. Handoff: monitor p99 threshold 1s, keep prefixhash rollout paused, don't resume until postmortem. Created incident ticket INC-2026-3307654321 and linked CS-6123.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete at 01:30:45Z — prefixhash set to v3 across all prod shards.

opsbot: Telemetry snapshot at 01:40: p95=260ms, p99=720ms, cache hitrate=84%. Paging ops back to baseline.

maria: great. Actions assigned: (1) postmortem draft (maria, dmitri) (2) runtime change review for hash seed change (kevin) (3) stronger rollout guard for prefixkey monotonicity (eng-runtime).

maria: handing off to dmitri for monitoring and postmortem follow-up. If p99 > 1s, escalate to oncall lead and page infra.

dmitri: ack. I'll keep a 30min cadence for metric checks and update this thread.

maria: thanks team — closing live triage. Final note: consider adding canary-level prefetch key verification step to rollout pipeline to avoid namespace flips. :white_check_mark:
